briefings.title: AI Compute: Rebuilt for the Agentic Era | Mark Papermaster, AMD | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: AMD is pivoting from a component manufacturer to a holistic systems provider to meet the demands of "Agentic AI," which requires a rebalanced 1:1 ratio of CPUs to GPUs and an open-source ecosystem to ensure enterprise sovereignty and efficiency.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
AMD is pivoting from a component manufacturer to a holistic systems provider to meet the demands of "Agentic AI," which requires a rebalanced 1:1 ratio of CPUs to GPUs and an open-source ecosystem to ensure enterprise sovereignty and efficiency.

## The Shift to Agentic Workflows and Productivity
* **From Serial to Parallel:** Mark Papermaster notes that AI is transitioning from simple chatbots to agentic workflows that orchestrate many parallel tasks simultaneously, replacing old serial processes in manufacturing, accounting, and tech.
* **Massive Productivity Gains:** Unlike previous tech inflections (PC, Mobile) that offered incremental gains, Agentic AI is delivering "game-changing" results.
    * At AMD, AI tools have reduced the time required for new chip features from months to mere weeks or days.
* **The "Reasoning" Requirement:** Modern models with high reasoning capabilities require massive context windows, necessitating a complete rethink of how hardware handles complex prompts.

## Re-Architecting the Hardware Stack
* **The Rise of the CPU in AI:** While GPUs handle the "matrix thinking," the CPU’s role has expanded to manage the orchestration, reasoning, and complex prompts of agentic agents.
    * **Ratio Shift:** Historically, the industry used a ratio of one CPU to eight GPUs (1:8). In the agentic era, this is shifting toward a 1:1 ratio.
* **Holistic Design:** AMD has moved away from siloed CPU and GPU divisions in favor of "holistic design," where networking, compute, and software are optimized as a single system to eliminate bottlenecks.
* **Edge and Personal AI:** Efficiency is being driven by moving compute to where the data lives.
    * **Strix Halo:** A new PC platform designed to run 100-billion-parameter models locally and efficiently.
    * **Factory Floor AI:** Analyzing data at the source to compress the amount of information that needs to be sent to large data center clusters.

## Strategic Acquisitions and Open Standards
* **ZT Systems Acquisition:** AMD acquired ZT Systems to offer fully optimized rack-level solutions rather than just individual chips.
* **Commitment to Openness:** Papermaster argues that AMD’s "open ecosystem" approach is a primary differentiator against closed-source competitors. 
    * **European Sovereignty:** Open standards are critical for European enterprises and regulators who wish to avoid vendor lock-in and maintain control over their data and models.
    * **Collaborative Blueprinting:** AMD provides blueprints for its "Helios" AI racks to manufacturing partners rather than competing with them, speeding up the overall time-to-market for the industry.
* **Energy Efficiency:** With the world "energy gated," AMD is focusing on driving higher utilization of existing compute infrastructure through better software orchestration to ensure AI remains economically viable for CFOs.

## AMD’s Internal Evolution and Roadmap
* **Corporate Culture:** Papermaster describes AMD’s "secret sauce" as a combination of a "scrappy underdog" fighter mentality and a disciplined culture of execution.
* **AI-Native Operations:** All 33,000 AMD employees, including the entire sales force, have been trained in AI and are currently writing their own agents to optimize internal workflows.
* **Upcoming Innovations:**
    * **Helios AI Rack:** A 72-node rack utilizing open OCP standards for CPU, GPU, and networking.
    * **Venice CPUs:** Upcoming 2-nanometer architecture designed for next-generation performance.

> "We’re going from productivity gains that we had prior to the last 6 months of 10%... to now dramatic improvements. In our own chip design at AMD, we’re shaving months off time to market." — Mark Papermaster

> "The role of CPUs used to be a headnote controller for my GPU. Now, with bigger and bigger context windows... it is literally becoming one CPU to one GPU." — Mark Papermaster

> "AI is just not an option for any of us... you’ll be left behind if you’re not adopting. Our goal is to think like a startup. If there is an AI-native startup, how would they go about solving that problem? That’s what we want to do." — Mark Papermaster

briefings.title: AI Has a Power Problem: Why the U.S. Power Grid Can't Keep Up | The Real Eisman Playbook Ep 69
briefings.tldr: The U.S. power grid is the primary bottleneck for AI expansion, requiring roughly 30 gigawatts of new capacity annually through 2035 to meet surging demand from data centers, manufacturing onshoring, and aging infrastructure.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The U.S. power grid is the primary bottleneck for AI expansion, requiring roughly 30 gigawatts of new capacity annually through 2035 to meet surging demand from data centers, manufacturing onshoring, and aging infrastructure.

## The Looming Grid Crisis & Data Center Demand
* **The Scale of the Problem:** The U.S. grid currently generates roughly 150 gigawatts (GW) of electricity. Estimates suggest the country needs between 100 and 350 GW of new capacity by 2035.
    * **Annual Growth:** The grid needs to add approximately 30 GW of capacity per year over the next decade.
    * **The "Lumpy" Buildout:** Data center development is constrained by labor shortages and power availability. While many projects are announced, actual construction is lumpy due to permitting and interconnect delays.
* **Technological Shifts:** The industry is moving toward an 800-volt architecture for new Nvidia chips, which requires more sophisticated power electronics and grid equipment.
* **Beyond Data Centers:** While AI gets the headlines, the grid is under stress from "onshoring" manufacturing, the electrification of homes/vehicles, and the decommissioning of 75-year-old coal plants.

## GE Vernova (GEV) and the Infrastructure "Super Cycle"
* **The "Long Tail" Business:** GE Vernova is a primary beneficiary of the grid expansion. Their Power segment, which sells massive natural gas turbines, is currently booked out through 2030–2031.
* **Electrification Segment:** Beyond turbines, GEV sells high-voltage equipment and transformers. They are successfully cross-selling this "nuts and bolts" equipment directly into data center projects.
* **Nuclear Outlook:** GEV is partnering with Hitachi on Small Modular Reactors (SMRs). 
    * **Timeline:** These 300MW reactors are unlikely to move the needle on earnings until the late 2030s. The first project in Ontario is targeted for 2035.
* **Wind Power:** Currently viewed as a "call option" or "self-help" story, as the company works through legacy offshore wind projects that have been financially taxing.

## The Tesla and SpaceX Strategic Outlook
* **The Tesla Energy Story:** The energy business—specifically "MegaPacks" (large-scale batteries for the grid)—now accounts for 20% of Tesla’s operating income and is growing at 30% annually.
* **The SpaceX Acquisition Theory:** Analyst Ben Kallo predicts SpaceX may eventually acquire Tesla.
    * **Strategic Control:** Elon Musk has expressed a desire for 25% ownership to control Tesla’s AI development; an acquisition via SpaceX (where he has high ownership) would facilitate this.
    * **Speed of Decision-Making:** Combining boards would allow for faster execution on joint projects like the proposed 100 GW solar module facility.
* **Autonomous Driving:** Despite years of delays, Tesla’s "vision-only" (camera-based) approach allows for faster scaling than competitors like Waymo, as Tesla harvests data from its entire existing vehicle fleet.

## Broader Mobility, Solar, and Raw Materials
* **EV Market Competitors:** 
    * **Rivian:** Positioned as the "first follower" of Tesla. The upcoming R2 model (approx. $45,000) is viewed as a compelling alternative to the Tesla Model Y.
    * **Lucid:** Currently viewed more as a technology provider than a mass-scale manufacturer, buoyed by Saudi Arabian investment.
* **The Solar Dilemma:** Kallo avoids residential solar due to high customer acquisition costs ($10,000 per home). 
    * **First Solar (FSLR):** Stock performance is currently tied to looming U.S. tariff decisions on Chinese components. If strict tariffs are implemented, there is a projected $100 upside to the stock.
* **Critical Minerals:** MP Materials (Rare Earths) is highlighted as a critical play for domestic supply chains, as China currently controls 90%+ of the magnet market required for EV motors and data center HVAC fans.

> "The range of estimates [for new capacity] could be 100 gigawatts needed by 2035 up to 350. At 350, you're more than doubling all the electricity generation in the United States." — **Ben Kallo**

> "If the only business that Tesla had was the electronic vehicle business, the stock's way overvalued." — **Steve Eisman**

> "We have a decade of visibility here. The CEO of GE Vernova talks about it being a super cycle and that they expect to be sold out to 2035 at least." — **Ben Kallo**

briefings.title: AI Is the New Operating Environment. Data Is the New Control Plane. | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: In the AI arms race, competitive advantage is defined by the compression of time—specifically the time required to deploy infrastructure, orchestrate global data, and feed GPUs at peak velocity.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
In the AI arms race, competitive advantage is defined by the compression of time—specifically the time required to deploy infrastructure, orchestrate global data, and feed GPUs at peak velocity. By moving from legacy "two-dimensional" storage protocols to a "three-dimensional" Linux-native control plane, organizations can eliminate hardware bottlenecks and treat data as a routed resource.

## The Three Critical Time Frames of AI Performance
David Flynn identifies three distinct windows of time that determine an organization's success in the AI "arms race":

*   **Token Generation Velocity:** The speed at which GPUs generate tokens is often constrained by the time it takes to load state from storage. High-velocity data delivery is essential for maximizing GPU utilization.
*   **Infrastructure Lead Times:** Deploying new physical storage can take 3 to 6 months due to hardware shortages. Hammerspace advocates for a software-defined approach that virtualizes existing storage to bypass these procurement delays.
*   **Data Orchestration & Movement:** Traditional data copying between data centers is too slow. Organizations need a single logical file system that is eventually consistent across multiple locations, allowing data to be consumed as soon as it is generated, regardless of where it resides.

## From Flat Earth to 3D: Data as a Routed Resource
Flynn argues that the industry must move beyond the limitations of legacy storage networking.

*   **2D vs. 3D Architectures:** 
    *   **2D (Legacy):** A simple client-server connection where all data must pass through a specific server proxy, creating "congested intersections" and bottlenecks.
    *   **3D (Modern):** A control plane architecture where the client receives routing information to make direct, parallel connections to any data item in the environment.
*   **Linux-Native Integration:** By building the "plumbing" for parallel file systems directly into the Linux kernel (using the NFS standard), Hammerspace allows data to become a "routed resource" without requiring custom software agents or exotic HPC clients.
*   **Leveraging Existing Assets:** This architecture allows companies to use the NVMe storage already built into GPU servers as part of the overall file system, rather than buying dedicated "tier one" storage.

## The Economics of the Global Flash Shortage
The "SSD crisis" is fundamentally changing how AI infrastructure must be built.

*   **The HBM Competition:** Flash/NAND manufacturers are prioritizing High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) fabs over traditional SSD production because the margins are higher. Consequently, the shortage of high-performance flash is expected to persist.
*   **The Hybrid Resurgence:** Because high-performance flash is scarce, hybrid systems—combining SSD, Hard Disk Drives (HDD), and even Tape—are becoming essential. 
*   **Efficiency through Parallelism:** A native parallel file system in Linux is more efficient at aggregating performance from slower media (like HDDs), allowing organizations to achieve "brute force" flash speeds using more available, cost-effective hardware.

## Strategic Implementation: Reducing Deployment Friction
To compete, organizations must reduce the "human effort" and "manpower" involved in data management.

*   **Eliminating Migrations:** By using a data orchestration layer to virtualize existing storage nodes, companies can avoid the downtime and risks associated with massive data migrations.
*   **Standardization:** Using the NFS standard ensures that the system is plug-and-play with modern Linux environments, which have already won the "OS war" in the hyperscale and HPC sectors.
*   **Software-First Delivery:** Reducing the setup time from months to days is achieved by treating data logistics as a software problem rather than a hardware shipping problem.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "In the AI arms race, because it is an arms race... the central thing, the thing which matters more than anything else, is time. How much time it takes." — **David Flynn**

> "The original storage networking protocols were let's say two-dimensional... kind of like being stuck on flat Earth, where you have to go through congested intersections in a busy city street. [We are] moving to where you have three-dimensional, you can talk to a control plane, and then make direct connections to any of many targets." — **David Flynn**

> "Hybrid systems are here to stay. Even tape is having a resurgence... because that's not competing for the same manufacturing fabs as [high bandwidth] memory." — **David Flynn**

briefings.title: AI, Security & Economic Power: A New Playbook for Democracies | Sebastian Kurz | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: To maintain global relevance, democracies must transition from a regulatory-first mindset to an "ecosystem-based" sovereignty that prioritizes massive capex investment, energy abundance, and localized control over security-critical AI infrastructure.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
To maintain global relevance, democracies must transition from a regulatory-first mindset to an "ecosystem-based" sovereignty that prioritizes massive capex investment, energy abundance, and localized control over security-critical AI infrastructure.

## Redefining AI Sovereignty: Ecosystems vs. Isolation
* **The Ecosystem Model:** Jacob Helberg argues that true sovereignty is not about vertical integration or "rebuilding yesterday's technology" in-house, but being a net contributor to a global innovation ecosystem.
    * **Historical Precedent:** When the US missed the "5G boat," it did not attempt to build a domestic Nokia or Ericsson; instead, it became a massive buyer of allied technology while banning national security threats like Huawei.
* **The European Perspective:** Sebastian Kurz emphasizes that while 100% independence is impossible, the COVID-19 pandemic revealed the dangers of total dependency on China for basic goods. 
    * **The "Mythos" Moment:** Recent US restrictions on the "Mythos" AI model served as a wake-up call for Europe, highlighting that a foreign government can unilaterally decide whether European companies remain customers of foundational technology.
* **Strategic Autonomy:** Kurz suggests Europe should focus sovereignty efforts on "on-prem" solutions for sensitive sectors, including government data, financial systems, and national security, rather than trying to compete in every consumer-facing foundational model.

## Security, Intelligence, and "Dream"
* **Hybrid Warfare:** Sebastian Kurz’s new venture, **Dream**, focuses on AI-based cybersecurity and data analysis for nations and critical infrastructure. 
    * **The New Superpower Metrics:** Kurz posits that while nuclear capabilities defined superpowers in the past, modern power is derived from AI, Cyber, and eventually Quantum capabilities.
    * **Current Scale:** Dream is roughly three and a half years old and has reached a valuation/funding level of $3 billion, aiming to help non-superpowers achieve "superpower" status in digital defense.
* **Responsible Release:** Helberg clarified the US government’s stance on restricting powerful models, noting the goal is a "30-day window" for security evaluation to prevent mass cyberattacks on critical infrastructure before a general release.

## Economic Security and Industrial Reality
* **The "Facebook Ads" Fallacy:** Helberg warns that digital sovereignty is meaningless without industrial sovereignty, noting that the war in Ukraine proves that "you can't win a war with Facebook ads; you need drones, bullets, and factories."
* **China's Dominance:** The discussion highlighted alarming statistics regarding dependencies on China:
    * **Rare Earths:** China controls 90% to 99% of the market.
    * **Smartphones:** China controls 50% to 85% of the global market.
    * **Automotive:** Chinese manufacturers are increasingly "crushing" the traditional European and American automobile industries.
* **The AI Economic Engine:** In the US, the AI boom is driving 2–3% GDP growth and hundreds of billions in capex, keeping unemployment below 5% despite energy market volatility.

## A Policy Playbook for Democracies
* **US Strategic Pillars:** Helberg outlines the current US "playbook" for AI leadership:
    * **Capex Expensing:** Allowing companies to benefit from accelerated depreciation on massive technology investments.
    * **Energy Abundance:** Lowering the cost of AI compute by expanding domestic energy production, including drilling in Anoir and the Gulf of Mexico.
    * **Permitting Reform:** Streamlining the NEPA process to allow builders to move faster.
* **The "Draghi" Warning for Europe:** Helberg cites Mario Draghi’s report, noting that the EU has gone "way too far" on regulation. 
    * **Regulatory Friction:** The **Digital Markets Act (DMA)** is cited as the source of 80% of friction between the US and EU, with US officials viewing it as a "non-tariff trade barrier" designed to extract money from wealthy American firms.
* **Mindset Shift:** Kurz argues that Europe’s primary obstacle is its mindset. He asserts that Europe has lost its focus on competitiveness and must realize that without being an economic leader in AI, it will be unable to finance its social welfare systems in the future.

> "You have people nowadays that are busy throwing Angry Birds at pigs on their cell phones while riding an 18th-century subway... You can’t win a war with Facebook ads. You need drones and bullets and factories."
> — **Jacob Helberg**

> "We were used to being the customer on many products... with the 'Mythos moment,' for the first time people realized we will not be able to be the customers if another government decides we can't. If we do the same mistake in the field of AI [that we did in tech previously], it will be a disaster for Europe."
> — **Sebastian Kurz**

> "Competitiveness is the reason to be economically successful... and without being economically strong, you cannot finance the social welfare system and everything that a lot of people enjoy in Europe."
> — **Sebastian Kurz**

briefings.title: Andrew Ng and David S. Goyer: Creativity, Intelligence, and What We’re building Toward.

people.name: Andrew Ng
people.role: AI Researcher and Founder of DeepLearning.AI

briefings.tldr: AI integration in creative and technological industries requires keeping "humans in the lead," balancing open-weight innovation against closed gatekeeping, and separating media hype from the practical realities of automation and software development.
briefings.summary_markdown:
## TL;DR
AI integration in creative and technological industries requires keeping "humans in the lead," balancing open-weight innovation against closed gatekeeping, and separating media hype from the practical realities of automation and software development.

## AI Narratives, Hype, and the Labor Market
* **The Hype Cycle vs. Reality:** **Andrew Ng** asserts that tech companies historically stoked extinction and job-loss fears as PR stunts to inflate valuations. Controlled lab tests (like AI blackmail scenarios) are exaggerated by media in ways analogous to testing an airplane in a hurricane.
* **The 1.4% Employment Reality:** Citing a workforce management CEO's survey on recent layoffs, **Andrew Ng** notes that only **1.4%** of recently laid-off workers were actually replaced by AI. 
* **Task Automation:** Studies show AI can automate **30% to 40%** of discrete tasks in many jobs, but the remaining **60% to 70%** requires human execution, historically leading to higher wages and complementary job growth (similar to horses transitioning to cars).
* **The 15-Year-Old Skepticism:** **David S. Goyer** points out that many young people (including his 15-year-old son) are violently opposed to AI out of fear of being squeezed out of jobs, leading to commencement booing and career self-selection away from tech.

## Open Weights vs. Proprietary Gatekeepers
* **Defining Open Weights:** **Andrew Ng** explains that open-weight models publish the foundational list of numerical weights on the internet for free download (allowing local execution on personal laptops), whereas closed-weight models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google Gemini) hide the weights behind a proprietary API.
* **China's Open-Weight Strategy:** **Andrew Ng** notes that while U.S. models lead in closed-weight capabilities, China leads in open-weight models. Nations in Africa and elsewhere widely adopt Chinese models over American ones, which serves as a massive vehicle for foreign soft power and ideological influence (e.g., answering questions about Tiananmen Square in 1989).
* **The Danger of Gatekeepers:** **Andrew Ng** warns that if AI concentrates in the hands of a very small number of gatekeepers (analogous to Android and iOS in mobile), everyone except the gatekeepers will be worse off.

## Hollywood, Creativity, and Workflow Integration
* **Human in the Lead vs. Loop:** **David S. Goyer** stresses that creators must remain "human in the lead" rather than outsourcing creativity. Using basic prompts yields clichéd slop, but iterative workflows yield powerful results.
* **Goyer's Production Workflow:** **David S. Goyer** shares that on projects like *Foundation* Season 2, he and his visual effects supervisor used **Midjourney** early on for wild, unexpected concept design iterations before handing concepts to human artists. In writing, he uses AI to shorten a four-page monologue down to a two-page version across six variations, or to brainstorm cabin items for a high-end commercial helicopter action sequence, reducing feature draft times from **8 to 10 weeks** down to **4 to 5 weeks**.
* **Hollywood's Negative Narratives:** **Andrew Ng** laments that Hollywood produces predominantly negative, terminator-style AI stories, which discourages students from pursuing AI careers—contrasting it with positive entrepreneurial narratives promoted in China.

## Copyright, Bias, and Data Distortion
* **Plato’s Cave and Internet Distortion:** **David S. Goyer** raises concerns that models are trained on a digitized internet that is a distorted, biased representation of reality. **Andrew Ng** acknowledges this bias but counters that AI teams actively squash racist and sexist text, making current models *less* biased than the average human being.
* **The Copyright Lawsuit:** **David S. Goyer** notes he was part of a copyright lawsuit against Anthropic for using digitized books without permission, which he defines as crossing a distinct line compared to human learning. **Andrew Ng** compares AI learning from public internet pages to young artists copying old masters at museums, though he acknowledges long-term economic compensation models for publishers still need to be resolved.

## Predictions & Forward Calls
* **Andrew Ng** predicts that higher education's process for adapting curricula is too slow, leaving universities training students for the jobs of 2022 rather than 2028 or 2030 and beyond.
* **David S. Goyer** predicts that entertainment will permanently split into two tiers: content that is barely "human in the loop" versus content where humans remain firmly "in the lead."

## Notable Quotes
> *"The funny thing that happened was a handful of companies decided that stoking fear about AI was wonderful PR because it turns out that if you go around and say my technology is so powerful, I could cause the extinction of the human race. That turns out to be one way to convince people your technology is really powerful and therefore must be worth a lot."* — **Andrew Ng**

> *"You can't outsource your creativity if you want to create anything of any note... I think we're quickly moving to a place... where there's really going to be two tiers of art. There's going to be the stuff that's basically just barely human in the loop, and then there's going to be stuff that's human in the lead."* — **David S. Goyer**

> *"When someone asks a question of AI, such as what happened in Tiananmen Square in 1989? Well, whose model they are using will cause the model to give an answer that reflects that nation's values. So getting your stuff out there is a tremendous source of soft power influence."* — **Andrew Ng**

briefings.title: CJ Desai, MongoDB & Laura Modiano, OpenAI in Conversation | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: As AI-native applications scale, the data layer must evolve from a secondary consideration to a high-performance, flexible partner that scales in tandem with AI models to move beyond the "prototype treadmill" into production.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR** 
As AI-native applications scale, the data layer must evolve from a secondary consideration to a high-performance, flexible partner that scales in tandem with AI models to move beyond the "prototype treadmill" into production.

## The Data Layer as the "Unsung Hero" of AI
*   **The Scaling Paradox:** Founders often focus exclusively on application logic and model selection (e.g., OpenAI), treating the data layer as an implicit, secondary decision. 
    *   As applications scale, many "easy" initial database choices "choke" under performance demands, necessitating a data layer that can grow "humongously" alongside the model.
*   **Architectural Synchronization:** AI models and data layers must scale in tandem. CJ Desai emphasizes that MongoDB’s architecture is designed to support this "real-time applications data layer" for both AI natives like ElevenLabs and legacy giants like JPMorgan Chase.
*   **The 70/30 Rule:** To maintain human-centric relationships in a transactional industry, Desai follows a 70% listening and 30% talking rule to identify where founders are struggling with talent, infrastructure gaps, or sudden spikes in volume.

## The Evolution of the "Builder" and "Vibe-Coding"
*   **The Rise of the Polymath:** Tools like OpenAI’s Codex have fundamentally changed who can build, shifting the role from traditional developers to "polymaths" who use multifaceted skills to create applications via natural language.
*   **Vibe-Coding:** Desai cites *Immersive*, a platform that grew from $0 to $100M ARR in eight months by allowing builders to create CRM or logistics apps using natural language and "minimal moving parts."
*   **The Necessity of Schemaless Design:** Rigid infrastructure prevents AI agents from moving fast. 
    *   Because models (like the anticipated OpenAI 5.6) and application demands evolve rapidly, the underlying data layer must be schemaless to avoid becoming a bottleneck to innovation.

## A Strategic Framework for AI ROI
For enterprises to move from experimentation to production, Desai proposes a four-pillar framework to measure AI success:
*   **Innovate Faster:** Using tools like Codex to "shift-left" the product roadmap and accelerate new product creation.
*   **Sell More:** Utilizing AI to increase sales velocity and provide better intelligence to go-to-market teams.
*   **Serve Better:** Empowering customer success teams with proactive diagnostics and AI-driven support tools.
*   **Operational Efficiency:** Driving internal productivity to ensure the company remains "AI-forward" while managing the increased costs of AI infrastructure.

## Transitioning from Prototype to Production
*   **The Production High Ground:** In 2026, the focus has shifted from "prompting" to "production." Desai argues that Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) is the critical ground for agentic applications.
*   **Unified Data Layers:** Rather than managing fragmented systems, Desai advocates for integrating auto-embeddings, vector databases, and operational data into a single layer.
*   **Hybrid Multicloud & Sovereignty:** Especially in the European market, the ability to run AI applications anywhere—on-prem, in private environments, or across multiple public clouds—is essential for meeting data sovereignty and French/EU regulations.

***

**Notable Quotes**

> "When you truly try to scale [an] application, that’s when you find out that between your models and data layer, they both need to scale in tandem with each other." — **CJ Desai**

> "If you are rigid on the infrastructure software that you're using as a founder, what happens is then agents that you're building have to deal with that rigidity and you cannot move fast." — **CJ Desai**

> "From prompting to production or prototyping to production—this is the year to really figure out how do you create production systems at scale." — **CJ Desai**

> "The DNA of a builder... stays the same, but tools like Codex have completely fundamentally changed who is a builder, how they are a builder... [from] a developer to a polymath." — **Laura Modiano**

briefings.title: Data is Back: MongoDB, Databricks, Snowflake
briefings.tldr: Data has returned to the forefront of the AI cycle as the essential foundation for agentic applications, while hyperscaler capacity constraints and data sovereignty requirements are unexpectedly pushing large-scale AI workloads back to on-premise environments.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
Data has returned to the forefront of the AI cycle as the essential foundation for agentic applications, while hyperscaler capacity constraints and data sovereignty requirements are unexpectedly pushing large-scale AI workloads back to on-premise environments.

## The Resurgence of On-Premise and Sovereign AI
*   **Hyperscaler Capacity Limits:** Major cloud providers are reaching physical capacity limits. 
    *   CJ Desai cites a Fortune 100 customer in Texas that was denied additional cloud capacity despite being a "top 50" customer, forcing them to re-commission their own data centers for AI workloads.
*   **Data Sovereignty:** In regions like France, strict regulations and privacy concerns are driving a shift away from public clouds toward on-premise infrastructure.
*   **The Multi-Cloud Hedge:** Frontier labs and AI natives are increasingly adopting MongoDB because of its ability to run across multiple clouds (AWS, GCP, Azure), providing resiliency and avoiding vendor lock-in.

## MongoDB’s Role in the AI Stack
*   **Operational vs. Analytical Data:** Desai clarifies the market distinction between MongoDB and competitors like Snowflake or Databricks.
    *   **Real-time OLTP:** MongoDB handles "online transaction processing" (real-time interactions, credit card transactions, and agent memory).
    *   **Analytical OLAP:** Snowflake and Databricks focus on offline business analysis and "asking questions" of historical data.
*   **The Memory Layer for Agents:** MongoDB is being used as the "memory" for agentic workflows.
    *   **Scale Example:** ElevenLabs currently runs over 50 million agents on MongoDB.
    *   **Physical AI:** Robotics companies are using the database to store real-time sensory and action data generated by robots in the field.
*   **Frontier Lab Adoption:** Major AI labs use MongoDB for inference, voice products, and video/image creation due to its document-based architecture and ability to handle unstructured data.

## The Complexity of Enterprise Agentic Architecture
*   **Exploding Architectural Complexity:** A major bank's "agentic architecture" recently showed 55+ distinct components—including various LLMs, frameworks, and guardrails—compared to half that number just a year ago.
*   **Deterministic Outcomes:** In regulated industries like insurance, agents must provide deterministic results. Companies are building complex "human-in-the-loop" systems to audit agent decisions for bias and regulatory compliance.
*   **Shift in Labor Needs:** Modern AI companies refuse to hire traditional Database Administrators (DBAs). They demand "machine-based administration" and auto-scaling capabilities so engineers can focus on models rather than infrastructure.

## CEO Strategy and the Pace of Innovation
*   **Customer-Obsessed Cadence:** Desai maintains a pace of 10–12 individual customer meetings per week to ensure the product roadmap pivots in real-time based on scaling pain points.
*   **Software Writing Software:** The speed of innovation is accelerating because AI is now writing code, significantly lowering the incremental cost of experimentation and product development.
*   **Operational Agility:** Desai highlights that "speed is paramount," noting that even the most established companies are pivoting their AI strategies every 8–12 weeks as new models and frameworks emerge.

## Notable Quotes
> "Data is the unsung hero and data is back. You cannot create an AI application without a great data layer, and your AI application is as good as your data." — **CJ Desai, CEO of MongoDB**

> "You see these hyperscalers, some of them are running out of capacity... the hyperscaler said, 'Sorry, we don't have a capacity.' And they are one of the top 50 customers for that hyperscaler." — **CJ Desai, CEO of MongoDB**

> "I have never seen a pace like this... the incremental cost of innovation has gone down because software is writing software." — **CJ Desai, CEO of MongoDB**

> "In the database world when I was at Oracle, the most expensive person you can get is a DBA. Now these AI companies are saying: 'We don't have time to hire these people. If we are using your software, it should have its own machine-based database administration.'" — **CJ Desai, CEO of MongoDB**

**TL;DR**
The Trump administration is seeking an $87.6 billion supplemental funding package—as part of a broader $1.5 trillion defense goal—to sustain the ongoing conflict with Iran, replenish depleted munition stockpiles, and provide emergency relief to an agricultural sector crippled by high input costs and trade disruptions.

## National Defense and the Iran Conflict
*   **"Operation Epic Fury" & Readiness:** Secretary Hegseth characterized the supplemental as a "generational investment" required to fix years of "gross negligence" and deferred maintenance.
    *   **Conflict Costs:** The administration currently estimates the cost of the Iran war at $35 billion through the end of the fiscal year.
    *   **Strategic Assets:** General Caine emphasized that the character of war is changing rapidly, necessitating immediate investment in AI, autonomous systems, and "space dominance" to counter adversaries like China and Russia.
*   **Munitions Rebuilding:** The request includes $46 billion for high-demand munitions, solid rocket motors, and hypersonics.
    *   **Industrial Base:** Hegseth noted the department is cutting "multi-year procurement" deals to allow private companies to build their own factories, potentially doubling or tripling production speeds.
*   **The Strait of Hormuz:** Despite claims that Iran's conventional navy was "decimated," the Strait remains contested. Hegseth defended the administration's naval blockade and "blacklisting" of Iranian ships to stabilize global oil flow.

## Agricultural Crisis and Food Security
*   **Economic Distress:** Secretary Rollins reported that farm production costs rose significantly (fuel up 33%, fertilizer up 30%) while commodity prices plummeted, resulting in a $50 billion agricultural trade deficit. 
*   **Supplemental Relief:** The request includes $10 billion in temporary economic assistance for row and specialty crop producers to provide a "bridge" while the administration pursues long-term trade and regulatory reforms.
*   **Strategic Independence:** Rollins argued that "food security is national security," highlighting the danger of 85% of U.S. meat packing being controlled by four companies, including foreign-owned entities.
    *   **Reshoring:** The USDA is prioritizing the domestic production of fertilizer and seed to reduce reliance on "hostile countries."
*   **Biofuels:** Senator Rounds and Secretary Rollins advocated for permanent, year-round sales of E15 ethanol to lower prices at the pump and support corn growers.

## Congressional Critique and Oversight
*   **Unauthorized Warfare:** Vice Chair Murray and Senator Murkowski sharply criticized President Trump for initiating the Iran war without Congressional authorization or a clear coalition of allies.
    *   **Human Cost:** Critics noted that 17 American service members have died in the conflict, with hundreds more injured.
*   **Funding Disparities:** Several Senators (Padilla, Reed, Collins) questioned why the supplemental provides $1.1 billion for Florida freeze relief but excludes funding for California wildfires, New England crop losses, or New York/Rhode Island weather disasters.
    *   **"Red State" Bias:** Senator Reed alleged that 80% of disaster requests from "red states" are approved compared to only 20% from "blue states."
*   **Military Personnel Concerns:** Chair Collins expressed deep concern over the removal or sidelining of over 40 senior officers, noting that half were women or people of color, which she argued undermines the military's status as a meritocracy.
*   **Budget Management:** Senators questioned why the Department of Defense (DoD) is requesting new billions while still holding $75 billion in unspent funds from previous reconciliation bills.

## Notable Quotes
> "For almost 20 years, we had all of the time and almost none of the money. Today we have all of the money and no time."
> — **Gen. Dan Caine**, Chair of the Joint Chiefs of Staff

> "Either we invest in our warriors at this moment of step change on the battlefield and growing threats, or this is all just talk."
> — **Pete Hegseth**, Secretary of Defense

> "Farmers want to farm for their products and not for a government check. They want to be free from dependency and free to innovate."
> — **Brooke Rollins**, Agriculture Secretary

> "Tax dollars we could have spent helping people afford health care or building new housing have now been lit on fire by a president who blundered us into a disastrous war."
> — **Senator Patty Murray**, Vice Chair

briefings.title: In the Land of AI Agents, the Verifiers Are King — Tariq Shaukat, Sonar
briefings.tldr: While AI agents drastically increase development velocity, they also accelerate technical debt and security risks; to achieve enterprise-grade reliability, organizations must transition from a generation-focused approach to a "Guide, Verify, Solve" framework.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
While AI agents drastically increase development velocity, they also accelerate technical debt and security risks; to achieve enterprise-grade reliability, organizations must transition from a generation-focused approach to a "Guide, Verify, Solve" framework.

## The AI Productivity Paradox and "Slop"
*   **The Velocity Trap:** Research from Carnegie Mellon University indicates that the initial 3x to 5x boost in developer velocity provided by AI agents often dissipates within three months.
    *   **Technical Debt Accretion:** Gains are offset by a surge in security issues, maintainability hurdles, and increased code complexity.
    *   **The Hallucination Problem:** High-profile failures at firms like KPMG and EY demonstrate that while AI generates plausible-sounding output ("AI slop"), functional correctness does not guarantee enterprise-grade reliability.
*   **Accuracy vs. Complexity:** Benchmarking shows that while agents can handle complex 18-hour tasks, they currently do so at only a 50% success rate.
    *   When the required accuracy rate is raised to 80%, the complexity of tasks the agents can successfully complete drops from 18 hours to approximately 3.5 hours.

## The AC/DC Framework: Agent-Centric Development Cycle
*   **Shift in Focus:** Tariq Shaukat argues that verification must be baked into the process rather than treated as an afterthought. This is achieved through three specific disciplines:
*   **Guide (Preemptive Verification):** Providing agents with both "Context" and "Constraints."
    *   **Context:** Semantic maps and architectural awareness of existing codebases (even those with billions of lines).
    *   **Constraints:** Explicitly defining coding standards, forbidden dependencies, and "intended" (rather than just existing) architecture.
    *   **Efficiency Gains:** Proper guidance can result in a 30% reduction in token consumption by making the "territory" easier for the agent to navigate.
*   **Verify (Zero-Trust Model):** Implementing a multi-layered verification fabric that assumes every model has inherent biases.
    *   **Algorithmic Verification:** Using traditional tools to check data flows, control flows, and secrets.
    *   **Agentic Verification:** Using AI to check for intent, business logic, and "unknown unknowns."
    *   **Reliability Impact:** Organizations using multi-layered verification report 44% fewer AI-derived production outages.
*   **Solve (Verified Maintenance):** Actively using remediation agents to clean technical debt.

## The Three Loops of Continuous Verification
*   **The Agentic Loop:** Providing in-loop verification and constraints while the agent is actively generating code to reduce errors at the source.
*   **The CI Verification Loop:** Combining algorithmic and agentic reviews during the pull request (PR) process to maintain high-velocity quality gates.
*   **The Code Maintenance Loop:** A continuous improvement process focused on keeping the codebase "clean."
    *   **Machine Readability:** Contrary to the belief that agents don't care about code quality, clean codebases significantly reduce the reasoning, energy, and tokens required for agents to perform subsequent tasks.
    *   **Compounding Benefits:** One large bank achieved a 92% reduction in issues by applying this three-loop approach to their agentic workflows.

## Notable Quotes
> "I would still put someone who gave me 80% accurate information on a performance review... This isn't necessarily enterprise grade." — **Tariq Shaukat** (referencing a customer CTO)

> "You're building the technical debt as quickly as you are generating the code, or maybe even more quickly. And that creates a different set of work... a different bottleneck." — **Tariq Shaukat**

> "If you make the life of the agent easier, if you maintain your codebase, then you'll actually see compounding effects." — **Tariq Shaukat**

briefings.title: NVIDIA Keynote Live at SIGGRAPH 2026
briefings.tldr: NVIDIA unveiled DLSS 5 and the "Cosmos" world foundation model, signaling a fundamental shift where computer graphics and physical simulation are no longer just rendered by hand-coded algorithms, but generated and enriched by AI to train the next generation of autonomous robots.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
NVIDIA unveiled DLSS 5 and the "Cosmos" world foundation model, signaling a fundamental shift where computer graphics and physical simulation are no longer just rendered by hand-coded algorithms, but generated and enriched by AI to train the next generation of autonomous robots.

## DLSS 5: From Image Reconstruction to Neural Generation
Edward Liu (Director of Applied Deep Learning Research) introduced DLSS 5 as the next leap in real-time rendering, moving beyond "DLSS 4" path tracing into a purely generative era.

*   **Core Concept:** Unlike previous versions that focused on reconstructing pixels, DLSS 5 uses a one-step **Diffusion Transformer** model to "enrich" the appearance of a traditional render, adding photorealism that physics-based simulations struggle to compute in real time.
*   **Addressing Generative Hallucinations:** To prevent the AI from "improvising" (e.g., changing a character’s identity), DLSS 5 uses the game’s rendered frame as a rigorous, pixel-aligned signal rather than a text prompt.
*   **Technical Breakthroughs:**
    *   **Intent Preservation:** Uses internal buffers (albedos, normals) to ensure the AI respects the original artistic geometry.
    *   **Temporal Stability:** Operates frame-by-frame (causally) using motion vectors to eliminate shimmering or "drifting" common in video generation.
    *   **Efficiency:** Distills giant foundation models into a compact model that runs within a 16ms frame budget on consumer GPUs.
*   **The "Second Lever" for Quality:** Historically, image quality scaled with "rays and triangles." With DLSS 5, quality now scales with model size and training data, meaning image fidelity can improve without changing the underlying game engine.

## Granular Artistic Control in Neural Rendering
Creative Artist Gav demonstrated that DLSS 5 is not a "black box" filter but a controllable tool for art directors.

*   **Structure vs. Tone:**
    *   **Structure Intensity:** Modulates high-frequency details like ambient occlusion, subsurface scattering (e.g., light through ears/leaves), and contact shadows.
    *   **Tone Intensity:** Controls more expressive, low-frequency lighting and mood adjustments.
*   **Semantic Masking:** Developers can apply DLSS 5 selectively. A demo showed a kitchen scene where the AI enhanced translucency in glass bottles and reflections on a cutting board without affecting the rest of the environment.
*   **Model Mixing:** Artists are not locked into one "look"; different models (A, B, or C) can be used for different scenes or cutscenes to achieve specific visual targets.

## AI Physics: 1,000,000x Data Compression
Neil Ashton (NVIDIA AI Research Leader) detailed how AI is solving the "computational tax" of traditional physics-based simulations.

*   **Weather and Climate:** NVIDIA’s Earth-2 uses AI models (like StormScope) to predict complex storm patterns in seconds—tasks that previously required 20,000 GPUs running for hours.
*   **Computational Efficiency:**
    *   **Massive Compression:** Ashton demonstrated that 200 terabytes of high-fidelity aircraft simulation data can be compressed into a **200-megabyte model checkpoint**.
    *   **Speedup:** These models can predict airflow over unseen geometries with 98%+ accuracy in seconds, representing a 10,000x speedup over traditional solvers.
*   **Bridging Communities:** NVIDIA is calling for the SIGGRAPH community to apply differentiable physics and geometry modeling to structural engineering and electromagnetics.

## NVIDIA Cosmos: The Data Engine for Physical AI
Ming-Yu Liu (VP, Cosmos Lab) introduced Cosmos, a world foundation model designed to solve the data scarcity problem in robotics.

*   **"Compute is Data":** Because real-world robot data is slow to collect, Cosmos allows developers to "compute" synthetic, physics-aware environments (e.g., 1,000 different kitchens) for robots to learn in.
*   **The Mixture of Transformers (MoT) Architecture:** 
    *   **Autoregressive Tower:** Handles reasoning and language ("The Thinker").
    *   **Diffusion Tower:** Handles high-fidelity generation of pixels, audio, and actions ("The Creator").
*   **Action as a First-Class Modality:** Cosmos uses a common vocabulary of "geometric primitives" (egopose, gripper states). This allows the model to learn from *any* video—even human head-cam footage—and transfer that knowledge to a robot arm or a self-driving car.
*   **Model Family:**
    *   **Cosmos 3 Super:** High-accuracy frontier model.
    *   **Cosmos 3 Nano (16B):** Open starting point for developers.
    *   **Cosmos 3 Edge (4B):** Optimized for real-time performance on-device (Jetson Thor/RTX).
*   **Cosmos Dreams:** A new neural closed-loop simulator for autonomous vehicles. It generates a photorealistic, reactive world from a single frame, allowing a car to "drive in its own imagination" for policy verification.

## Notable Quotes

> "Simulation defines the world, generation enriches its appearance, and artists direct the outcome. This is not AI replacing graphics; it is AI extending graphics the same way programmable shaders and ray tracing did before." 
— **Edward Liu**

> "Physical AI has a data problem. Robots need to learn from the real world, but the real world only runs in real time. You cannot fast-forward reality. That is why world foundation models change the equation: data stops being something you collect; it becomes something you compute." 
— **Ming-Yu Liu**

> "It almost seems like magic, but it is true. We have around a million times compression—from 200 terabytes of data down to a 200-megabyte model checkpoint." 
— **Neil Ashton**

> "Artists and designers... have always invented technology in service of creativity. We want the power of AI, but grounded in 3D and governed by physics, so that it is shapeable by creators." 
— **Jensen Huang**

briefings.title: Powering AI Infrastructure: Solving the 21st Century Manhattan Project | RAISE Summit 2026
briefings.tldr: The defining engineering challenge of the decade is the rapid scaling of AI infrastructure, requiring a shift from 1.5GW to 10GW capacity per provider by 2027 while maintaining "Manhattan Project" levels of execution and transitioning from training-heavy labs to enterprise-scale inference.
briefings.summary_markdown:
**TL;DR**
The defining engineering challenge of the decade is the rapid scaling of AI infrastructure, requiring a shift from 1.5GW to 10GW capacity per provider by 2027 while maintaining "Manhattan Project" levels of execution and transitioning from training-heavy labs to enterprise-scale inference.

## The Mandate for Velocity and Execution
* **Exponential Scale:** Jeremie Eliahou Ontiveros (SemiAnalysis) highlighted that leaders like Anthropic are projected to grow from 1.5 gigawatts of capacity in 2025 to 10 gigawatts by 2027—a scale equivalent to today’s Google, but achieved in just two years.
* **Execution as a Differentiator:** Ben Richardson (CoreWeave) emphasized that speed is the primary market differentiator. Being "thoughtful but acting in concert" is essential; failure to operate at the speed of the fastest partner results in total project stagnation.
* **Capital Velocity:** CoreWeave’s open order book grew from $23 billion in March 2023 to $99 billion in March 2024, reflecting relentless global demand from model labs and hyperscalers.
* **The "Experience Gap":** Successful scaling requires institutional knowledge. Richardson noted that building two data centers provides some insight, but building four or more offers an "exponential" increase in necessary operational wisdom.

## Data Center and System Building Blocks
* **Vertical Integration:** Vik Malyala (Supermicro) stressed the "building block" approach, where servers, networking, and liquid cooling are validated as a single unit to minimize "time to online."
* **Interoperability and Open Standards:** Shaun O’Meara (Mirantis) argued for an "open API contract" between infrastructure layers. Because the hardware landscape changes every 6–18 months, infrastructure must be pluggable to avoid vendor lock-in and technical obsolescence.
* **Supply Chain and Readiness:** Data center readiness is currently a major bottleneck. Over 50% of projects face delays due to power delivery issues, permitting, or the shift from traditional voltage to 400V/800V DC busbars.
* **Heterogeneous Compute:** As the market matures, there is increasing demand for non-Nvidia alternatives. June Paik (FuriosaAI) noted that enterprises are seeking diversified supply chains and specialized inference chips to lower the Total Cost of Ownership (TCO).

## Networking and Simulation Challenges
* **Zero-Tolerance for Error:** Alex Saroyan (Netris) highlighted that networking is the "invisible" but most critical layer. Unlike traditional data centers, AI clusters have zero tolerance for configuration mistakes.
* **Digital Twin Technology:** To bypass hardware lead times, operators are increasingly using digital twins to simulate and validate network architectures before the physical hardware even arrives at the data center.
* **Modern Tooling:** Traditional scripting (e.g., Ansible) is often insufficient for the complexity of modern AI factories; specialized automation tools are required to manage the massive bandwidth and interconnect requirements.

## The Shift to Inference and Enterprise
* **Inference Dominance:** Shaun O’Meara predicted that 75% of all GPU workloads will be dedicated to inference by the end of 2027 as models move from development to production.
* **Enterprise ROI:** Enterprises are moving from public cloud "sandboxes" to on-prem or private cloud deployments to control costs and data sovereignty.
* **Local Execution in Europe:** Richardson noted that while the cloud is global, building is "distinctly local." Success in the European market requires navigating fragmented regulations and local power constraints rather than treating the continent as a single entity.

> "Building these systems is difficult... you’ve got to operate at the speed of the fastest. If there's one part of the system slowing you down, it's going to slow the entire system down."
> — **Ben Richardson, CoreWeave**

> "We are never going to be able to build an infrastructure today that's going to look the same way in 6, 12, or 18 months... we strongly believe one of the ways to move faster is to have open infrastructure."
> — **Shaun O’Meara, Mirantis**

> "The cost of running AI is getting to the point where it's becoming unsustainable in terms of energy and CapEx. We need a full-stack solution where every layer works together to make it more efficient."
> — **June Paik, FuriosaAI**

> "Networking is the one thing you don't see when AI is running right. But in these clusters, there is no room for error. You need specialized tools to go live this week, not in multiple years."
> — **Alex Saroyan, Netris**
